title: 2026 Semiconductor Industry Market Forecast - Slide Deck & Video Link Available
text:
Daniel Nenni

Watch the video recording and full slide deck NOW

Our Oct 6 IFS2026 industry update webinar reported that August saw two new records established: semiconductor sales broke through the $1tn barrier, while 36 consecutive months of month-on-month growth marked the longest period of sustained growth in the industry’s 70-plus-year history.

It also highlighted a return to growth in unit shipments, but cautioned that this growth could not be justified by underlying demand and was more likely the result of stockpiling, with another buildup of inventory potentially on the way.

We also warned ASPs were responsible for 90% of the dollar growth, continuing what has become a story of aberration, with ASPs reaching $4.13 in August — 30% higher than the next biggest previous peak, and that Capex spend — tomorrow’s new capacity — as a percentage of chip sales has finally fallen back below the long-term average trend line.

However, with sales numbers so inflated, capex spend remains high relative to real wafer fab requirements. China is also still spending more on capex than either Taiwan or Korea

With our revised 2025 forecast now at 125% growth, we warned against getting drunk on the numbers

While the figures are factual, they are seriously misleading, with non-AI datacentre-related growth still in the mid-single digits and analogue, discretes and opto yet to recover, although they have now stopped declining.
